lead.title: Abivax falls 17% in Paris after short seller Scorpion Capital attacks obefazimod weeks before its FDA filing
lead.deck: On November 20, Scorpion Capital, which disclosed a short position, branded Abivax's oral ulcerative colitis candidate a "toxin": it compared the drug's lipophilicity to that of banned pesticides, cited lab tests it commissioned itself suggesting photocarcinogenic risk, and questioned skin-safety monitoring and the reliance on Chinese studies. Abivax says the report contains "numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements", notes that some of the cited studies were funded by Scorpion, and maintains its plan to file with the FDA before year-end: a stress test for the most closely watched asset in French biotech, whose shares are down 48% since January.

milestone.title: CARsgen reports first human data for CT1182, a CD19/CD20 CAR-T made directly inside the patient's body
milestone.summary: A single intravenous infusion, with no lymphodepleting chemotherapy, generates CAR-T cells in situ via the CARvivo platform (proprietary viral envelopes and T-cell-specific promoters). Among six patients with relapsed B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (median of three prior lines), there were three complete and two partial responses, all ongoing at the October 31 cut-off, with cytokine release syndrome limited to grade 1 and no neurotoxicity (ICANS).
milestone.why: It is one of the first clinical proofs that in vivo CAR-T can deliver complete responses without a cell therapy factory or lymphodepletion, coming right after Pfizer's $330M-upfront deal with Starna. Caution: six patients and 3.2 months of median follow-up; CARsgen aims to file for a registrational trial in the first half of 2027.

brefsEurope.title: Evaxion refocuses on cancer vaccines and pauses its infectious disease and autoimmune programs
brefsEurope.summary: The Danish biotech is leaning on Phase II data from its personalized vaccine EVX-01 in advanced melanoma to focus its AI-Immunology platform on off-the-shelf vaccines EVX-04 and EVX-05, notably targeting endogenous retroviruses from the non-coding genome. Its preclinical infectious disease assets will only advance with a partner.

brefsEurope.title: Novartis targets 5% annual growth through 2031 and lifts peak sales for Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio by $4B
brefsEurope.summary: Kesimpta rises to $8B, Scemblix and Leqvio to $5B each, as the group faces "the largest loss-of-exclusivity impact in our history" (Entresto, Promacta). A comparable that also recalls recent setbacks: the Phase 3 failure of del-desiran from the Avidity buyout ($1.9B impairment) and suspended trials of its CAR-T rap-cel in autoimmune diseases.

brefsEurope.title: EIB lends Théa €150M for ophthalmology R&D and its European manufacturing base
brefsEurope.summary: The European Investment Bank's second loan after €50M in 2021, backed by the InvestEU guarantee, will fund new molecules, formulations and delivery systems (retinal diseases, rare inherited eye diseases, glaucoma, dry eye) and the Milan industrial site. The family-owned group posted €1.02B in revenue in 2025.

brefsIntl.title: FDA rejects Capricor's deramiocel in Duchenne muscular dystrophy for a second time
brefsIntl.summary: The agency found the data insufficient to establish "substantial evidence of effectiveness" and cited "serious data integrity violations" in the HOPE-3 trial (blinding breaches, statistical analysis plan changed after the fact). A signal of regulatory rigor for every cell therapy betting on functional endpoints in rare diseases.

brefsIntl.title: Combined with chemotherapy, Revolution Medicines' pan-RAS drug Rasonque hits a 61% response rate in first-line pancreatic cancer
brefsIntl.summary: In the Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 study (61 metastatic patients), presented at the ENA symposium in Barcelona, disease control exceeded 90%, median progression-free survival reached 12.8 months and 12-month survival nearly 77%, with no control arm. A label expansion will hinge on the Phase 3 RASolute 303, expected in 2028.

word.full: In vivo Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell therapy
word.fr: CAR-T made directly inside the patient's body
word.definition: Instead of collecting a patient's T cells, engineering them in a factory and infusing them back, doctors inject a vector that installs the CAR receptor in the T cells itself, inside the body.

parts.label: Delivery vector
parts.role: the vehicle: an envelope-modified lentivirus or a lipid (LNP) or polymeric nanoparticle that carries the genetic material through the bloodstream

parts.label: CAR cargo
parts.role: the gene or RNA encoding the chimeric receptor aimed at a tumor or autoimmune target (CD19, CD20, CD22…)

parts.label: T-cell targeting
parts.role: the address: a viral envelope, ligand or T-cell-specific promoter that avoids modifying other cells

how.t: The patient receives an intravenous infusion of the vector, with no apheresis and no manufacturing wait; some programs, such as CARsgen's CT1182, even skip lymphodepletion.
The vector recognizes circulating T cells and makes them express the CAR receptor, either durably (lentivirus) or transiently (RNA in LNPs).
The newly created CAR-T cells multiply on contact with their target and destroy the cells that carry it, for example malignant or autoreactive B cells.

word.why: In vivo CAR-T promises to turn a bespoke, costly therapy into an off-the-shelf injectable, opening up autoimmune diseases and broader patient access. Big Pharma is now paying top dollar for assets still in preclinical development (Pfizer's $330M upfront for three Starna programs), and the first human data are arriving (CARsgen, Umoja's IND): for a European VC, still-independent non-viral delivery platforms are the targets to watch.

startups.name: Alaya.bio
startups.use: Proprietary polymeric nanoparticle that reprograms T cells inside the body; co-founded in 2022 with CAR-T pioneer Michel Sadelain, still preclinical

startups.name: T-CURX
startups.use: University of Würzburg spin-off; $20M Series A first close led by BiomedVC for its non-viral CAR-Ts and its in vivo platform of non-viral vectors delivered by LNPs

startups.name: Umoja Biopharma
startups.use: VivoVec lentiviral platform; FDA IND clearance in July 2026 for UB-VV400, the first known CD22-directed in vivo CAR-T, in the Phase 1/2 VIBRANT-1 trial

startups.name: Starna Therapeutics
startups.use: Targeted LNPs and RNA technology; licensed three preclinical in vivo CAR-T programs in autoimmunity to Pfizer in November 2026 for $330M upfront
